answer: At each challenge, an agent must post a unique proof-of-work bound to its identity, and the network prices every new address at the full stake it would risk as a sybil. One operator spinning up a thousand clones would have to bury real capital behind each, so a relic of the old "free identity" trick becomes useless overnight. From the dawn of the epoch, registrations also require a human-weighted attestation; a forged sonnet of fabricated vouches cannot pass peers who spot the same stamp reused. Attackers pay stake plus proof cost per seat, and that bill grows faster than any reward.
